differences.what: Massing: three storeys over a raised basement at the photograph's heights (principal floor 1.65 m, the projection's top 9.45 m, the wall head 12.45 m) — the draft's were the rules' (T-2543)

Gable: the front carried up as a shaped Flemish gable over the whole front, swelling from a kneeler each side and drawn in to a pointed head under a finial at 17.0-17.5 m, in place of the draft's stepped boxes (T-2543)

Gable: the outline re-read on both sides at a tenth of a metre and redrawn: the swell a convex curve from 2.98 m out at 13.0 m to 1.83 at 14.5 m swinging in to the shoulders, where the draft stood 0.3-0.5 m wide of it, and the head a bell from 1.10 m at 15.3 m to 0.35 at 16.5 m on the finial's square plinth (0.48 m across from 16.65 m), which the draft drew as a point; the print's south side reads about 0.25 m wider than its north all the way up and the build takes the mean (T-2951)
Gable: the grid window nine lights, three rows of three about 0.44 by 0.37 m between stone mullions and over stone transoms, in the 1.64 by 1.26 m opening (T-2951)

Gable: its face on the wall's own plane, as the print's: the eave under it plain and 0.05 m deep, so the slab stands 0.07 m before the wall below, its foot just over the third storey's arches, with no eave, fascia or gutter across the front (T-2889)

Gable: each kneeler a carved scroll console at the front's corner (its roll from about 11.35 m, its body up to a cap under the slab's foot) under a small pinnacle on the ledge 3.85 m out, where the draft stood a plain square pinnacle (T-2951)
Gable: the shoulder stones square blocks 0.9-1.62 m out from 14.6 to 15.22 m, standing over the outline through the slab (T-2951)
Gable: each shoulder stone carries a sunk panel; built plain
Gable: the grid window stands in quoined side stones under a moulded hood with a wavy upper edge, over a deep moulded shelf; built with K06's own sill and no surround or hood
Gable: the grid window's lights read as dark openings; K06's casement frame reads heavier at 0.44 by 0.37 m
Gable: the kneelers' scrolls are carved; built as a plain roll with a raised eye
South projection: carried through the basement and two storeys to a flat top at the third floor, with the round-arched window, the basement light and the paired window in it (T-2543)

South projection: flush with the south corner, as the print's, its south cheek running on in the side wall's plane, and its north face kept on the print's (5.05 m out, the projection 5.05 m across where K08 had stood it 0.3 m in) (T-2953)

South projection: the barred basement light from the print's walk line up, over a 0.1 m plinth, the light 0.86 m clear to its head at 1.08 m, where K08 had kept it 0.65 m high over the 0.6 m plinth (T-2953)
Balcony: the iron balcony on the projection's top, round its cheeks and front, its rail about 0.5 m over the cornice as the print's (47 px both) and its balusters 0.24 m apart (T-2888)

Balcony: the middle of its front run (x 390-680 px) is a solid stone panel rising to a central pedestal, with iron scrolls against it; built as more of the iron rail, its balusters plain square bars without the print's roundels
South projection: its top, K08's 0.2 m fascia over the 9.45 m wall head, renders about 25-30 px over the print's cornice, and the balcony stands on it, about as high again

Third storey: the large window over the balcony under its flat segmental arch (2.78 m across, crown 12.05 m) with its fanlight, and the small round-arched window to its north (1.2 m, crown 12.0 m), each in a ring of voussoirs running up into the gable's face, the large one under its keystone (T-2889)
Second storey: the north window one wide window, 1.64 m across on a stone mullion, under a transom (T-2889)

Third storey: the large window's middle light is wider than the two beside it and carries an arched head of its own, and its fanlight has a concentric bar as well as radial ones; built as three equal lights under a radial fanlight
Third storey: the small arched window is filled with a patterned light or panel; built as a round fanlight sash
Third storey: the voussoirs alternate long and short into the brick; built as a ring of equal stones standing 0.1 m before the wall
Second storey: the north window's transom lights are glazed in small squares; built as one plate light each
Gable: from the kneelers (about 11.6-11.7 m) to the ledge (12.55 m) the slab's base runs out square past the side walls, where the print's outline is already drawing in

Entrance: the porch's broad arch, a segment 2.7 m across rising 0.79 m from its spring (4.28 m over the walk) to its crown (5.07 m; its ring's top 5.22 m), the transom at its spring and the segment over it glazed in three lights; under it the double door, a 0.29 m pier and the side light, 1.04 m across from a sill 0.56 m over the floor (T-2952)

Stair: the straight stair to the walk between solid stone cheeks, level 0.5 m over the landing and swept down to a block 1.1 m high at the foot, the landing run on north as a terrace behind a stone parapet pierced in two rows of square holes, the print's pierced panel at the landing (T-2952)

Entrance: the arch's south jamb and moulding run down the projection's north corner in the print (its outer moulding at about x 740-755 px), so the arch reads about 0.3 m further south and broader; the build stands its 2.7 m mouth clear of the projection, from 5.2 m

Entrance: the arch is turned in a narrow moulded ring of light stone, and its curve is flatter at the crown than a segment (nearer a half ellipse); built as K01's voussoir block on a segmental head with a keystone flush with the ring

Entrance: the transom under the fanlight is a heavy moulded beam about 0.25 m deep, and the fanlight's three lights are divided by narrow columns of small panes; built as K07's 0.07 m bar and three plain lights
Stair: the north cheek flares out as it sweeps down and both end in a carved newel under a cap; built straight, to a plain block

Fabric: a rock-faced stone basement to a smooth water table, the entrance bay's first storey in coursed stone up to the second floor's belt, and brick over it, banded and dressed in stone (the belts, sills, flat arches, voussoirs, the north window's quoined surround); the south projection brick over its rock-faced basement, its bands, sills, heads and reveals stone (T-2914)

Fabric: over the second storey's north window, from the projection's north face to the corner, the carved frieze (8.55-8.95 m) under a moulded band and the patterned band of sunk panels (9.15-9.63 m) under a ledge, and the carved bosses under the projection's second-storey jambs (T-2915)
Fabric: the projection's windows in quoined stone jambs, short and long in turn, and the band at the arched window's spring running from each corner to the arch (T-2915)
Carving: the frieze is an interlace of crossing straps and leaves and the bosses carved shields; built as T-2819's guilloche of rings and plain oval bosses in a moulded ring
South projection: the second storey's jamb stones rise past the window's head to small carved caps under the projection's cornice; built stopping at the head
Tone: the print's stone reads lighter than its brick; the built brown sandstone renders darker than the buff brick beside it (the colours are not shown, the relation is)

Downpipes down both ends of the front: the north one from a head under the north kneeler (10.3 m, the print's pipe top) down the main front's north end to grade; the south one down the projection's south corner from a head under its cornice to grade, and from a head under the south kneeler down the main front to the projection's top (T-2953)

Roof: a mansard behind the gable, in place of K01's 45-degree hip: straight steep slate faces (72 degrees, the north corner's lean, about 0.5 m out over 1.6 m of rise) from the side walls' heads at 12.45 m to a level curb at 14.45 m, the upper hip over it at 10 degrees and out of sight, so each shoulder shows a slate face laid in level courses under a level top; the north top renders at y 294-296 px against the print's cap at 302-313 (T-3033)

Roof: at the south the print's slate face ends in a vertical band (x 277-293 px) standing just outside the south wall's line (the build's corner, about x 305), from the slate's foot up to a heavier level cap at y 257-277 px, about 0.4 m over the north cap, with the tall stack standing on it: the south wall carried up past the curb as a coped parapet (the c. 1955 photograph sees the same coped top from the south, T-3034); built as the mansard's south face, its corner leaning in from x 305 to about 360 px and its top level with the north: the side-wall parapet is a kit change K01 does not make

South stack: Levy's shaft (x 262-318 px, top y 127) and the c. 1955 photograph's place it 1.35-2.35 m behind the main front, standing outside the south wall's line, topping 16.8 m; moved there from 6.1 m back at 17.59 m on K01's on_cornice stack, which stands it on the wall line, so it renders about 60 px north of the print's: the stack on the wall's outer face is the same kit change (L-k01-1812-wheeler-stacks-3034)
Colour: the print is monochrome, so every stone, brick and paint colour
The side and rear walls, which the photograph does not see
